channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Short-Term Effects of Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in Addition to Physiotherapy on Spasticity, Walking Performance, and Quality of Life in Chronic Stroke: A Sham-Controlled Randomized Trial.
item.description: Adding 4 weeks of radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy to physiotherapy significantly improved spasticity (-0.56 MAS, 95% CI -0.77 to -0.35), walking performance (-1.41 s 10MWT), motor function, and quality of life in chronic stroke patients, with no adverse events.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The effect of multimodal sensory therapy in consciousness improvement in patients with acquired brain injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (N=884) found that multimodal sensory therapy (MST) significantly improved consciousness levels (SMD, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.04-1.92) and increased the odds of coma emergence (OR, 9.85; 95% CI, 3.86-25.01) in adults with acquired brain injury-related disorders of consciousness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Video-based education is non-inferior to in-person education in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy: a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial | Archives of Physiotherapy
item.description: A non-inferiority RCT (n=166) found preoperative video-based education was non-inferior to postoperative in-person education for pain self-efficacy (PSEQ MD: -0.6, 1-sided 95% lower bound: -3.8 at T1) and led to reduced kinesiophobia (TSK) at 6 weeks post-surgery in patients undergoing arthroscopic partial meniscectomy.
item.author: Arch Physiother

item.title: Effects of a multicomponent exercise programme including high-intensity interval training in institutionalised older adults with probable sarcopenia: a multicentre randomised controlled trial
item.description: A multicenter RCT (n=92) found a 12-week multicomponent exercise program including HIIT significantly improved handgrip strength (mean difference: 9.11 [7.70 to 10.51]; p < 0.001) and physical performance (SPPB mean difference: 3.75 [2.93 to 4.56]; p < 0.001) in institutionalized older adults with probable sarcopenia, compared to a control group.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: Optimising Exercise Prescription: A Meta-Analysis Examining the Dose Response of Exercise Duration on Cardiorespiratory Fitness Following HIIT and MICT
item.description: A dose-response meta-analysis of 69 RCTs (n=2387) found HIIT elicited greater improvements in VO2max than MICT (d = 0.38, 95% CI 0.27–0.49, p < 0.001). HIIT showed a non-linear dose-response, with 80% of maximal effect achieved with ~11 min/session (95% CI 9.5–40.2).
item.author: Sports Medicine

item.title: Novel Telerehabilitation Interventions for Stress Urinary Incontinence : A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of 13 RCTs found telerehabilitation-delivered pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) to be a safe, feasible, and effective modality for stress urinary incontinence, offering comparable efficacy to active conventional care and superior outcomes to passive management, particularly in improving accessibility.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in adults with transfusion-dependent α-thalassaemia or β-thalassaemia (ENERGIZE-T): a double-blind, randomised, multicentre, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial
item.description: A phase 3 trial found mitapivat to be the first oral disease-modifying therapy for adults with transfusion-dependent α-thalassaemia or β-thalassaemia, significantly reducing transfusion burden with a favorable benefit-risk profile.
item.author: The Lancet

item.title: Fall-prevention education after achieving independent walking is associated with reduced subsequent fall risk in patients with stroke: a retrospective pre-post intervention study.
item.description: A retrospective pre-post intervention study (1,437 stroke patients) found that standardized fall-prevention education delivered immediately after achieving independent walking was associated with a significantly lower adjusted hazard of the first fall (aHR: 0.58, 95% CI: 0.43-0.76, P<.001) and a lower fall incidence rate (IRR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.51-0.90, P=.006).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of Sequential Electroacupuncture Combined With Augmented Reality Gait Training on Walking Function and Neuromuscular Control in Subacute Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A 4-week randomized controlled trial (n=40) in subacute stroke patients found that sequential electroacupuncture combined with augmented reality gait training significantly improved gait speed (P=0.011), stride length, gait symmetry, motor function, and balance compared to augmented reality alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical Exercise Reduces Fall-Related Outcomes Among People With Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (1536 participants) found that physical exercise significantly reduced the number of falls by 39% (IRR = 0.61, 95% CI = [0.47, 0.78]) among people with stroke, with balance training and integrated cognitive components being most effective.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Leader and Follower Roles in Adapted Tango Reveal Complementary Neural Routes to Motor Improvement in Parkinson's Disease
item.description: A 12-week randomized controlled trial found that adapted tango, in both Leader and Follower roles, significantly improved overall disease severity and motor impairment in people with mild-to-moderate Parkinson's disease, compared to a control group, suggesting complementary neural routes to motor improvement.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Biological effects of technique-specific manual therapy in healthy individuals and people with musculoskeletal disorders: a systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis (50 studies, 2,147 participants) found that manual therapy (MT) is associated with short-term modulation of neurophysiological regulation, with technique-specific response profiles. Joint mobilization primarily induces sympathetic-driven responses (increased skin conductance), while soft tissue techniques are more frequently associated with parasympathetic-driven markers (reduced heart rate, increased RMSSD).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adductor-Related Athletic Groin Pain: A Clinical Commentary.
item.description: A clinical commentary synthesizes current evidence on adductor-related athletic groin pain (ARAGP), highlighting risk factors (prior injury, reduced eccentric hip adduction strength), diagnostic imaging, and supporting progressive strengthening, eccentric loading, and neuromuscular training for rehabilitation and prevention.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of Music-Based Interventions in Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of nine studies found music-based interventions in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) primarily improved psychological outcomes, motivation, and exercise adherence, rather than direct cardiovascular parameters. The evidence suggests music serves as a supportive adjunct to CR, with further high-quality studies needed.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is therapeutic exercise as a standalone intervention effective in reducing kinesiophobia in adults with nonspecific chronic low back pain? A systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 8 RCTs (854 participants) found that standalone exercise significantly reduced kinesiophobia in adults with chronic nonspecific low back pain (MD = -5.38; 95% CI -7.63 to -3.13; SMD = -1.03), exceeding the minimal clinically important difference, despite considerable heterogeneity (I² ≈ 94%) and low certainty of evidence.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Load-dependent Motor Cortical Activation Assessed by fNIRS Is Partially Preserved After Stroke.
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 12 stroke patients and 12 healthy controls found that stroke patients retained proportional load-related hemodynamic responses in the ipsilesional posterior parietal cortex during upper limb lifting tasks, unlike healthy subjects who showed responses in multiple motor-related cortical regions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: REmotely monitored, Mobile health-supported Multidomain Rehabilitation with High Intensity Interval Training for COVID-19 (REMM-HIIT-CoV): Trial Design and Rationale.
item.description: This article describes the design and rationale for REMM-HIIT-CoV, a multicenter, single-blinded, attention-controlled RCT (N=140) evaluating a remotely monitored, mobile health-supported multidomain rehabilitation program incorporating high-intensity interval training for functional exercise capacity in community-dwelling adults post-COVID-19 hospitalization.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Perceptions and Experiences of Returning to Sport Following Myocardial Infarction: A Qualitative Study.
item.description: A qualitative study explored perceptions and experiences of 20 patients returning to sport after myocardial infarction, identifying challenges such as reconciling active identity with new reality, vulnerability, need for support, and navigating their own path.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Isolated anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction versus reconstruction with a lateral extra-articular procedure (LET or ALL reconstruction): a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 comparative studies found that combined ACLR with a lateral extra-articular procedure significantly favored augmentation for IKDC (MD = 2.24, 95% CI: 0.40 to 4.07, p = 0.0168) and Lysholm (MD = 2.08, 95% CI: 0.37 to 3.79, p = 0.0171), but these differences became non-significant after Holm correction.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation: a narrative review of clinical applications, proposed mechanisms, and implementation.
item.description: A narrative review on music-based interventions in adult stroke rehabilitation found consistent evidence for rhythmic auditory stimulation for gait and selected music-supported upper-limb programs, while other applications like melodic intonation therapy for aphasia show potential but require more research on everyday transfer.
item.author: PubMed
